sections.title: Divine Council and Judgment
observations: Psalm 82 opens with a striking image of God standing in the divine council, judging among the 'gods.' This term 'gods' refers to earthly rulers or judges who are expected to uphold justice and righteousness.

The psalmist emphasizes that God holds these leaders accountable for their actions, highlighting the seriousness of their responsibilities. The imagery suggests that God is not distant but actively involved in the affairs of humanity, particularly in matters of justice.

sections.title: The Call for Justice
observations: In this section, God rebukes the unjust rulers for their failure to defend the weak and the needy. The psalmist underscores the moral obligation of leaders to protect the vulnerable and to administer justice fairly.
This call for justice resonates with the broader biblical theme that God is a defender of the oppressed. It serves as a reminder that true leadership is characterized by compassion and righteousness.

sections.title: The Consequences of Injustice
observations: The psalm concludes with a sobering declaration of the fate awaiting these unjust rulers. Despite their status as 'gods,' they will die like mere mortals due to their failure to fulfill their divine mandate.

This serves as a warning that earthly power is temporary and that God’s judgment is inevitable. The psalmist encourages the audience to reflect on the nature of true authority and the accountability that comes with it.

importantVerses.commentary: How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked?
Nevertheless, you will die like mere mortals; you will fall like every other ruler.

questions: What does it mean for God to stand in the divine council, and how does this imagery affect our understanding of His authority?
In what ways can modern leaders learn from the rebuke given to the unjust rulers in this psalm?
How does the promise of judgment for unjust leaders encourage us to seek justice in our own communities?
